paragraphs: Rabbi Natan bar Abba (II). (In the third generation of the Amoraim of Eretz Israel.) In the Jerusalem Talmud, Moed Katan, chapter 3, end of halakha 1, it is related that Rabbi Shmuel bar Abba was a mourner, and Rabbi Elazar came to him; he had then pared his nails and did not cover them. But when Rabbi Natan bar Acha came to him, he covered them, and said to him: “And do you think that you are as dear to me as Rabbi Elazar?” Now this cannot be Rav Natan bar Abba, the disciple of Rav and Shmuel, for Rav Shmuel bar Abba was still younger than Rabbi Zeira, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: The supplied narrative has Natan bar Acha, while the heading has bar Abba; the checked passage has bar Abba. Shmuel covers his nail-cutting on Natan’s arrival, not on Elazar’s. The different name forms remain visible in the source.
